newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable in slow late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable in slow late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in slow late trading on Thursday as the central bank kept its fixing rate unchanged.
"Players were waiting for another suprise on the central bank's fixing policy this afternoon, but it has kept the rate unchanged," one Japanase bank dealer said.
The dealer said the policy to keep the rate unchanged had kept the rupiah moving in a narrow range.
Bank Indonesia surprised the market on Wednesday by raising its fixing for the second day in a row, suggesting it was serious about challenging players who wanted to test the band.
Dealers said relatively ample rupiah liquidity in the market also kept the rupiah within a narrow trading range.
They said spot rupiah was last quoted at 2,323.20/23.50 against an opening of 2,323.00/24.00.
Rupiah liquidity on Friday, however, was unlikely to be as ample as on Thursday due to expected corporate tax payments and large SBPU maturities, dealers said.
One European bank dealer said sharp rises in the tom/next swap rate on Thursday reflected a higher demand for the local currency on Friday.
Tom/next swap rose to 2.10/2.30 from 1.60/1.70. Overnight swap was last at 0.10/0.30 against an opening of 0.30/0.40.
One-month swap was quoted at 17.5/18.5, two at 35.50/36.0, three at 52.0/53.0 and six at 103.0/104.0 points.
The local bank dealer said the dollar-rupiah rate was expected to range between 2,323.0 and 2,324.5 on Friday.
The cental bank, Bank Indonesia, maintained its intervention rate at 2,322.00/2,514.00 and the conversion rate.
